title: Session compression and action-id handshake for resumable streaming (PRD draft)
content:
Purpose and high-level problem statement:

This is a working PRD for a complementary set of features intended to make Hosted API streaming more robust on flaky mobile networks, reduce client-visible retransmit waste, and provide deterministic semantics for tool-calls and structured outputs when sessions are resumed. We combine two core ideas: compact session compression (delta/frame-level compression plus compact checkpoints) and an action-id handshake (per-action stable identifiers + reconciliation rules). Goal is pragmatic: ship a minimal first iteration that reduces token replays and developer complexity for SDK integrators while keeping server runtime changes modest.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Streaming API semantics changes (optional backwards-compatible extensions)
- Wire-level delta compression and compact session checkpoints
- Action-id assignment and reconciliation for tool calls and structured outputs
- SDK ergonomics: snapshotting, automatic resume, and developer observable APIs
- Observability and rollout/telemetry plan
- Backwards compatibility, migration story, and open questions

Non-goals:
- Large runtime rearchitecture (we aim to reuse existing stream framing and persistence where possible)
- Full client offline-first SDK (we only add lightweight snapshot/resume primitives)

Why this matters (motivation / user stories):
- Mobile product: users on intermittent networks see duplicated tool invocations when clients reconnect and re-submit the same request. This creates dangerous side effects (duplicate orders, duplicate emails) for customers using tool-calls.
- Low bandwidth: long transcripts re-sent on resume are expensive. Delta compression plus checkpoints can dramatically cut repeated token transfer for resumed sessions.
- Developer ergonomics: today customers implement idempotency ad-hoc (nonce-based, server side matching) which leaks implementation complexity. Action-ids offer a canonical approach for hosted-tool idempotency and result reconciliation.

Key concepts and terminology:
- Session snapshot: a compact serialized state representing the last committed application-visible frames (structured outputs, action metadata, final output tokens up to a checkpoint).
- Delta frame: a stream frame encoding only the delta since last checkpoint (diff of JSON fields and token index ranges).
- Checkpoint: a server-generated durable point that can be requested by client; material for resume. Checkpoints have a stable checkpoint_id and byte range pointers into persisted KV cache.
- Action-id: short stable identifier assigned to discrete actions returned in the stream (e.g., tool calls, function invokes, step frames). Clients can provide a client-generated id; if absent, server will assign. Action-ids are used to dedupe and to map partial responses across resumes.

Design proposals (high-level):
1) Wire-level optional headers (backwards-compatible):
   - New handshake flags on session create: "resumeable=true" and "snapshot_frequency="N"" (optional).
   - Streaming frames carry: frame_id, seq_no, optional action_id, checkpoint_hint (boolean), and a compressed payload blob.
   - Payload formats supported: plain text tokens, JSON partials, compact-delta (RLE+field diffs). Server advertises supported compression algorithms in handshake (e.g., "zstd-lite", "delta-json-v1").

2) Checkpoint lifecycle:
   - Checkpoints are created at configurable cadence (time or tokens) and at deterministic action boundaries (after tool_call returns).
   - Checkpoints stored in durable object store with checkpoint_id. Client can request resume with latest checkpoint_id; if omitted server will pick most recent for that session.
   - Checkpoint granularity: small (every 2–4s), medium (20–60s) depending on customer profile; default: medium.
   - Each checkpoint contains: last_committed_action_ids (list), truncated token offset, compact snapshot of structured output state.

3) Action-id contract and reconciliation rules:
   - Clients MAY include an optional client_action_id when calling the API (string). If not provided server will attribute a server_action_id.
content_continued:
- Server guarantees monotonic action sequence per session: action_n -> action_n+1. Action-ids are globally unique per session and are stable across resume if the underlying action result is considered committed.
   - Deduplication: on resume, server compares incoming client_action_ids with checkpoint.last_committed_action_ids and will suppress re-execution of actions already committed. For tool-calls with side effects the server returns a 2xx event indicating "replayed" plus original result, not re-run.
   - Partial outputs: action frames may be partial (e.g., function signature then args then result). Partial fragments carry same action_id so client libraries can reconstruct.

SDK ergonomics (developer-facing primitives):
- Lightweight SessionManager class (JS/Go/Python): handles handshake, local snapshot store, automatic resume, and exposes simple callbacks: onResume, onReplayPrevented, onCheckpointSaved.
- API examples (pseudocode):
  - createSession({ resumeable: true, snapshot_frequency: 20 }) -> sessionToken
  - stream(sessionToken, { client_action_id: 'ui-1234' }) -> streaming events with action_id fields
  - SessionManager.on('disconnect', autoSaveLocalSnapshot)
  - SessionManager.resume({ checkpoint_id: last_local_id }) -> returns a stable stream starting at checkpoint
- Developer ergonomics notes: SDK should default to transparently deduping tool-calls when client provides client_action_id; developer opt-out option available. SDK should also provide simple helpers to render "replayed" events in UIs (small banner) so product teams can decide to notify end users.

Server implementation notes (engineering impact):
- Minimal server changes: persist checkpoints in existing KV (no new global service). Add metadata per session: latest_checkpoint_id, last_committed_action_ids (small array).
- Stream framing: reuse existing compact frame format but add optional compression codec field and action_id header.
- Tool runner integration: before invoking side-effecting tool, check checkpoint.last_committed_action_ids to avoid duplicates. If present, return cached result with "replayed" flag.
- Latency considerations: compression adds CPU; provide "zstd-lite" option that targets mobile low-CPU. Many clients will prefer "no compression" for low-latency paths.

Observability and telemetry:
- New metrics to emit: checkpoint_create_rate, resume_success_rate, resume_replay_prevented_count, action_dedup_rate, compression_savings_bytes (per session), avg_resume_bytes_transferred.
- Trace spans: record checkpoint.id and action_id as attributes. Provide direct links from console trace to checkpoint payload for debugging.

Rollout plan (phased):
1) Internal alpha: small subset of internal services and infra team uses experimental SDK to surface corner cases (2–3 weeks).
2) Beta opt-in: announce to customers as "resumeable streaming" opt-in flag with SDK 0.x release. Enable default checkpoint frequency = 60s. Collect telemetry. (4–6 weeks)
3) Default enablement and tuning: after telemetry and a migration guide, flip default to enabled for mobile user agents with snapshot_frequency = 20s for specific plans. (8–12 weeks)

Backwards compatibility and migration story:
- Connectors that do not speak compression or action-id will continue to work: server will stream uncompressed frames and will not attempt dedupe by client_action_id (server_action_id still created but client cannot proactively dedupe without SDK).
- Existing customers that have built idempotency layers can adopt client_action_id to integrate with server-side dedupe for a simpler approach.

Security and compliance considerations:
- Checkpoint payloads may contain PII or customer data. Checkpoints will be encrypted at rest and governed by the existing KMS/HSM flow for hosted API.
- Checkpoint retention defaults follow current session retention policy; offer shorter retention for high-security customers.

Open questions (quick list):
- How to handle forks: if a client resumes from an older checkpoint then sends a different set of client_action_ids for actions that conflict with checkpointed committed actions, do we allow branching (fork) with new action sequence or reject? Proposal: reject by default and surface clear "conflict" response with guidance; allow advanced opt-in branching semantics later.
- Compression tradeoff: what set of codecs should be supported out-of-the-box? Zstd-lite vs diff-based JSON. Need benchmarks on mobile CPU cost.
- Checkpoint frequency default: what should be billing impact if checkpoints are stored more frequently? Will customers be charged for checkpoint storage?

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: server state growth from retained checkpoints. Mitigation: garbage-collect old checkpoints once a session is closed or after retention TTL; tune default TTL to 24–72 hours for resumed sessions.
- Risk: SDK complexity across languages. Mitigation: implement core behavior in JS and Go (most used), provide reference Python and a clear wire contract so customers can reimplement if needed.

Next steps / TODOs (owners):
- Implement wire format doc and update streaming API spec (owner: Jonas) [2w]
- Prototype checkpoint persistence in staging, measure storage and CPU (owner: Ethan) [3w]
- Build SDK SessionManager prototype in JS, integrate with internal mobile app (owner: Priya) [3w]
- Run 2-week alpha with internal users and capture telemetry (owner: Claire) [4w]

Appendix: minimal example (illustrative)
- Handshake response sample (json-like):
  {
    "session_id": "s_abc123",
    "resumeable": true,
    "compression": ["identity","zstd-lite"],
    "checkpoint_policy": {"frequency_s": 20} 
  }
- Sample streaming frames: (frame headers simplified)
  frame{frame_id=10, seq=10, action_id="act-23", payload_compression="zstd-lite", payload=<<compressed-json-delta>>} // partial structured update
  frame{frame_id=11, seq=11, checkpoint_hint=true, checkpoint_id="cp_42"} // durable checkpoint created after action commit

Notes on uniqueness: this doc intentionally centers on combining compact session checkpoints with explicit action identifiers to provide deterministic resume semantics and to reduce duplicate tool execution. It focuses on mobile and low‑bandwidth constraints and prescribes a pragmatic SDK abstraction (SessionManager) rather than a full offline-first overhaul.

End of draft.
